title: pytest
bridge: A pytest fixture is like a beforeEach that returns a value, and a test asks for it by parameter name. Except: fixtures have scopes (one per test, or one per session) and can depend on each other. Tests are plain functions found by their name, not registered with test().
intro: G7 builds a new cloud test layer on pytest. It uses fixtures for the fakes, xdist for parallel runs, testmon for affected tests, and markers for contract suites. This lesson gives you the pytest words those tickets use. You already know Vitest; most of this maps one to one.

picture.caption: pytest finds test functions, builds the fixtures they name, and with -n splits them across worker processes.

steps.text: collects every test_*.py file and every function named test_*
reads the parameter names of each test and finds a fixture with that name
with -n 2, starts two processes and hands each a share of the tests
each worker runs its tests; assert failures become the summary

sections.h: A test file next to a Vitest file
p: In Vitest you write describe, it and expect. In pytest a test is a function whose name starts with test_, in a file whose name starts with test_. The check is the plain assert keyword. When it fails, pytest rewrites the assert so the message shows both sides, like expect(a).toBe(b) does.
Below are the tests for the Money class from p10-1. Three ideas are in this one file: a fixture, pytest.raises and parametrize.
sections.because: You will read tests like these in tests_api, so every pytest word should be tied to a line you have seen.

notes.text: The parameter ten_shekels is not passed by anyone. pytest sees the name, finds a fixture called ten_shekels and calls it.
A plain assert. On failure pytest prints the values on both sides of ==.
pytest.raises is expect(fn).toThrow(). The with block is a context manager: it runs the block and checks what happened at the end.
parametrize is it.each. The decorator names the parameters, then gives one tuple per case.
This one function becomes three tests, named test_format_money[1000-10.00 ILS] and so on.

p: A fixture is a function with the @pytest.fixture decorator. Its return value is what the test receives.
Put it in the test file to use it there. Put it in conftest.py to share it with every test in that folder and below. pytest loads conftest.py by itself; nobody imports it.

A fixture can clean up: write yield instead of return, and the lines after yield run when the test ends. That is afterEach in the same function. A fixture can ask for other fixtures by name, so builder can ask for api_client, which asks for the database.

Scope decides how often the fixture runs. The default is function: once per test. scope="session" runs it once for the whole run; G7-02 uses that for the database setup. pytest ships useful fixtures: tmp_path (a fresh folder), monkeypatch (change an attribute or env var, undone after the test), capsys (captured output).
sections.because: Every fake in G7 arrives in a test through a fixture. Most of them patch something with monkeypatch and undo it after the test.

notes.text: The decorator registers the function as a fixture. Its name is what tests ask for.
A fixture can have a return annotation; it documents what tests get.
A fixture that asks for another fixture (monkeypatch, built in) by naming it as a parameter.
setattr replaces a module attribute for this test only. G7-05 does the same to swap AWSStorageServiceProvider for the in-memory store.
yield hands control to the test. Code after yield is cleanup.

callout.text: Changing the imported name (from lab1.money import DEFAULT_CURRENCY) patches nothing, because the test module holds its own copy. Patch the attribute on the module that reads it, as G7-05 patches storage_service.AWSStorageServiceProvider.

p: A marker is a label on a test: @pytest.mark.contract. Run only those with pytest -m contract, or skip them with -m "not contract". G7-02 registers two markers for the new layer, contract and sdk_smoke, and G7-29 adds quarantine(ticket=...). pytest-django adds django_db, which you will use in p10-3.

Register markers in the config file, or pytest warns about an unknown mark. The config file is pytest.ini (or a [tool.pytest.ini_options] table in pyproject.toml). It also sets pythonpath, which fixes most import errors.
sections.because: CI selects the contract suites and the SDK smoke tests by marker. So you need to know where markers come from.

code.text:
[pytest]
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = rhinoCloud.rhinoDjango.settings
django_find_project = false
pythonpath = ../.. ../../../common ../rhinoCore/integration-tests
markers =
    contract: runs the same checks against the fake and the real service
    sdk_smoke: the published rhino-health SDK against this commit's API

notes.text: pytest-django reads this to configure Django before the tests (p10-3).
Folders added to sys.path, relative to this file. This is why from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore... imports work.
Each registered marker, one per line, with a short description. Unregistered marks give a warning.

sections.h: Run tests in parallel with xdist
p: pytest-xdist adds -n. pytest -n 4 starts four worker processes and shares the tests between them.
-n auto uses one per CPU. Each worker is a separate Python process with its own memory, so tests that share a global or a file will collide. Tests must each build what they need.

Inside a test or fixture, the worker_id fixture tells you which worker you are on. It is gw0, gw1, or master when xdist is off. G7-02 uses it to give each worker its own database copy. The cloud CI job runs pytest tests_api -n 4.
sections.because: The API layer is meant to run in about 3 minutes locally, and that number assumes -n 4.
sections.ifInstead: If instead some tests pass alone and fail with -n, two tests share state. That could be a file, a global or a database row. Find the shared thing and give each test its own, with tmp_path or a fixture.

sections.h: Run only the affected tests with testmon
p: pytest-testmon records which lines of your code each test executed, in a file called .testmondata. On the next run with --testmon it looks at what changed and runs only the tests that touched those lines. The first run runs everything and writes the data. A run with nothing changed runs nothing.
This is what G7-13 wraps as poe api-test-affected, so an agent in the sandbox gets an answer in under 30 seconds. testmon only sees Python code that tests execute.

It cannot see migrations, fixture files or conftest setup, so when those change, G7-14's poe verify runs the full layer instead. Do testmon and -n combine for the pinned version? Check the testmon docs before you add -n to that task.
sections.because: Fast feedback for agents depends on running the small affected set, and you need to know what testmon can and cannot see.
sections.see:
$ uv run pytest --testmon -q
.....                                                                    [100%]
5 passed in 0.05s
$ uv run pytest --testmon -q
no tests ran in 0.00s
sections.ifInstead: If instead every run still runs every test, .testmondata was not written. Check that the file exists next to pytest.ini. It should be ignored by git, not missing, so look on disk, not in git status.

sections.h: Reading a failure and rerunning one test
p: A failure prints the test's node id (file::function[case]), the assert with both values, and the traceback. Rerun one test by its node id. --lf reruns only the tests that failed last time.

-x stops at the first failure. -k word selects tests whose name contains the word. --tb=short cuts the traceback to the lines that matter. --durations=10 lists the slowest tests, which G7-27 asks for.

G7-12 adds a plugin that writes reports/failures.md. For each failing test it lists the file and line and the first error line. Then the last 40 lines of the traceback and a rerun command. That one page is what an agent reads instead of a 3,000-line log. The same ticket fixes the random seed with pytest-randomly, so a failure reproduces with the same order.
sections.because: An agent fixes a failure only when the failure is short and complete, and the same is true for you.
sections.see:
$ uv run pytest -q --tb=short
.....F                                                                   [100%]
________________________________ test_rounding _________________________________
tests/test_broken.py:5: in test_rounding
    assert format_money(Money(5)) == "0.5 ILS"
E   AssertionError: assert '0.05 ILS' == '0.5 ILS'
FAILED tests/test_broken.py::test_rounding - AssertionError: assert '0.05 ILS...
1 failed, 5 passed in 0.01s
sections.ifInstead: If instead the summary says ERROR, not FAILED, the failure happened in a fixture or in setup, not in the test body. Read the fixture named in the error first.

sections.h: Two runners live side by side in fcp
p: The cloud's existing unit tests (about 1,900 in rhinoCore/tests and rhinoTaskServices/tests) run with Django's own runner. That is manage.py test --parallel 4, with CommonRhinoTestCase and factory_boy. They are not pytest tests and stay that way. The integration tests in rhinoCore/integration-tests are pytest, run against shared QA.

G7-01 decides the split. Tests that call an endpoint and check the response go to the new tests_api layer (pytest, pytest-django, xdist). Model and service unit tests stay in rhinoCore/tests. When you add a test to the cloud, this decision tells you which folder and which runner.

lab.title: pytest with fixtures, -n and testmon

worked.do: cd lab1 && uv add --dev pytest pytest-xdist pytest-testmon
Create tests/conftest.py with the ten_shekels fixture, and tests/test_money.py with the three tests from the first section.
uv run pytest --testmon -q && uv run pytest --testmon -q
worked.see:
5 passed in 0.05s
no tests ran in 0.00s

worked.do: Change the ValueError message in money.py, then: uv run pytest --testmon -q
worked.see: Only the tests that execute add() run: 2 passed (the three format tests are skipped by testmon).

lab.faded: Add tests/test_broken.py with one test that asserts format_money(Money(5)) == "0.5 ILS" (wrong on purpose). Run uv run pytest -q --tb=short and read the failure: file, line, both values. Then run only that test by its node id, fix the expected value, and run --lf. The node id command is the step left for you.
lab.alone: Add a fixture tickets in conftest.py that returns three Ticket objects from p10-1's faded lab. Add a parametrized test that checks total_days for lists of one, two and three of them. Register a marker slow in a pytest.ini and put it on one test. Run pytest -m "not slow" and confirm one test is deselected.
lab.done: pytest -q passes, and pytest -n 2 shows two workers. The second --testmon run says no tests ran, and -m "not slow" deselects exactly one test.

quiz.q: A test is declared def test_upload(object_store, builder). Where do object_store and builder come from?

options.text: pytest finds fixtures with those names in the test file or a conftest.py above it and calls them.
options.why: Fixtures are matched by parameter name; nobody passes them by hand.

options.text: The test module must import them from conftest.py.
options.why: conftest.py is loaded by pytest itself; importing from it is a common mistake that breaks fixture scoping.

options.text: pytest passes None for parameters it does not know.
options.why: An unknown name is an error: fixture 'builder' not found.

quiz.q: You run pytest -n 4 and a test that always passed now fails with a KeyError inside a shared dict. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: xdist runs tests in a random order and the dict was empty.
options.why: Order is not the issue; separate processes are. Each worker has its own copy of the dict.

options.text: Two tests share state that one of them set up in the same process; with workers that setup happened in another process.
options.why: Workers are separate processes with separate memory. Each test must build what it needs.
It supports any Python; it only changes which process runs which test.

quiz.q: After a change to a migration file, poe api-test-affected (testmon) reports no tests ran. Why, and what does G7-14 do about it?

options.text: testmon has a bug; rerun it.
options.why: It works as designed: it tracks executed test code, not files read during setup.

options.text: Migrations run during database setup, not inside a test, so testmon never saw them. poe verify runs the full layer when migrations or fixtures change.
options.why: This is exactly the FULL_RUN list in scripts/poe_verify.py.
The template database runs every migration; the tests depend on them.

words.plain: A function pytest calls to build a value a test asks for by parameter name. yield in it means cleanup after the test.
A file pytest loads by itself; fixtures in it are shared by every test in that folder and below.
A decorator that turns one test function into one test per row of cases, like it.each.
A label on a test (@pytest.mark.contract) that -m selects; registered in pytest.ini.
One of the separate processes -n starts; each runs a share of the tests with its own memory.
A plugin that remembers which code each test ran and reruns only the tests touched by a change.
The full name of one test, file::function[case], used to rerun exactly that test.

tickets.why: Its conftest is a session-scoped django_db_setup fixture that uses worker_id, both explained here.
The failures.md plugin hooks pytest_sessionfinish and reads the node id and traceback of each failed test.
poe api-test-affected is pytest --testmon, with the limits this lesson names.
The quarantine marker is a registered marker turned into a non-strict xfail at collection time.

remember: Tests are test_ functions, fixtures arrive by parameter name, -n runs them in processes, --testmon runs only what a change touched.
